question.prompt: What is the greatest possible area of the triangle in the complex plane with vertices \(2z,\) \((1+i)z,\) and \((1-i)z,\) where \(z\) is a complex number satisfying \(|4z - 2| = 1?\)

solutions.title: Scale a fixed triangle
solutions.explanation:
All three vertices contain the same factor \(z\), so their triangle is similar to a fixed triangle. This lets us separate its shape from its size.

Multiplying complex numbers multiplies their moduli: \(|zw|=|z||w|\). This follows by expanding the real and imaginary parts and squaring. Consequently, multiplying every vertex by \(z\) multiplies every distance between vertices by \(|z|\).

The triangle with vertices \(2,1+i,1-i\) has a vertical base of length \(2\) and a corresponding height of \(1\), so its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot2\cdot1=1.
\]
Similar triangles have areas in the square of their side-length ratio. Thus the requested triangle has area \(|z|^2\).

Rewrite the constraint as
\[
\left|z-\frac12\right|=\frac14.
\]
It describes a circle centered at \(\frac12\) with radius \(\frac14\). The distance from the origin to any point on this circle is at most
\[
|z|\leq\frac12+\frac14=\frac34.
\]
Equality occurs at the allowed value \(z=\frac34\). Therefore the greatest area is
\[
\boxed{\frac9{16}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

solutions.title: Compute with real coordinates
solutions.explanation:
Writing \(z=a+bi\) turns both the area and the constraint into expressions involving \(a\) and \(b\).

The three vertices have coordinates
\[
A=(2a,2b),\qquad B=(a-b,a+b),\qquad C=(a+b,b-a).
\]
The coordinate vectors from \(A\) to the other vertices are
\[
B-A=(-a-b,a-b),\qquad C-A=(b-a,-a-b).
\]
For vectors \((p,q)\) and \((r,t)\) from one vertex, the triangle area is \(\frac12|pt-qr|\), the triangle case of the shoelace formula. Here the area is
\[
\frac12\left|(-a-b)^2-(a-b)(b-a)\right|
=\frac12\bigl((a+b)^2+(a-b)^2\bigr)
=a^2+b^2.
\]
Meanwhile, the constraint gives
\[
(4a-2)^2+16b^2=1,
\qquad
\left(a-\frac12\right)^2+b^2=\frac1{16}.
\]
Expanding the last equation shows that
\[
a^2+b^2=a-\frac3{16}.
\]
The circle equation also gives \(a\leq\frac34\), so the area is at most
\[
\frac34-\frac3{16}=\frac9{16}.
\]
This value is attained when \(a=\frac34\) and \(b=0\), which satisfy the constraint. The greatest area is therefore \(\boxed{\frac9{16}}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
